text: This capstone uses every major piece of this course on one project — a governed lakehouse that ingests streaming orders and a daily catalog batch, transforms both, and holds up to an audit.

Five steps, in order: Unity Catalog structure, Auto Loader ingestion for both stream and batch, a Lakeflow pipeline for transformation, a multi-task Job for orchestration, and performance plus security applied throughout.
The governance shape gets decided before any ingestion code — one catalog, bronze/silver/gold schemas, and a volume for the daily file drop, all managed tables.
Two ingestion problems, two configurations — directory-listing Auto Loader for the stream, trigger-once batch mode with schema evolution for the daily catalog export.
Bronze to silver to gold, declared, with data quality inline. A bad order total gets dropped without halting the pipeline; a missing customer ID gets tracked but kept.
One multi-task Job chains the batch ingestion, pipeline run, metrics refresh, and failure notification. The streaming ingestion runs as its own separate job entirely.
A broadcast-join candidate in the gold layer, liquid clustering for time-range queries, a column mask on customer email, a managed identity, and audit logging throughout.
Nothing here is a new concept — every piece came from Chapters 1 through 6. What's new is making them all work together on one real system.
